lessons.title: Pass a lambda through a functional interface
lessons.summary: What happens if offset is reassigned after the lambda is created?
explanation: A functional interface has one abstract method. IntUnaryOperator accepts one int and returns an int through applyAsInt. In x -> x + offset, x is the input; the expression is the returned result.
A captured local variable must be final or effectively final: not reassigned after initialization. This restriction is on the binding, not a promise that a referenced object is immutable.
Expected output or behavior: 7. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Replace the capture with a literal and predict the result. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

lessons.summary: What prints if the requested key changes from 3 to 9?
explanation: String::length here is an unbound instance method reference: each incoming String becomes the receiver on which length() is called. lessons.title: Work with dates and time zones
lessons.summary: If the instant is 12:30 UTC the same day, what two dates print?
explanation: Instant represents a point on the time line. A ZoneId supplies rules for presenting that point as a local date and time. LocalDate alone contains no zone or time-of-day.

At 00:30 UTC on January 1, New York is still on December 31. Converting the instant with atZone preserves the instant, not the displayed calendar date. Region zones carry daylight-saving rules; fixed UTC does not shift seasonally.

2024-12-31. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

lessons.title: Calculate decimal amounts deliberately
lessons.summary: If the numerator is 2.00, what prints?
explanation: BigDecimal is immutable. Constructing from "0.10" keeps that decimal value; constructing from a binary floating-point double can expose its approximation. Arithmetic returns a new value.

Dividing 1.00 by 3 cannot produce a finite exact decimal. This example asks for two fractional digits and HALF_UP rounding, producing 0.33. HALF_UP chooses the nearest value, with exact halfway ties rounded away from zero. A positive scale specifies the number of digits to the right of the decimal point; it is not the same as a significant-digit precision. Currency rules must be chosen for the actual domain.
Expected output or behavior: 0.33. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

lessons.title: Make a defensive immutable snapshot
lessons.summary: If copyOf is replaced by unmodifiableList, what prints?
explanation: List.copyOf makes an unmodifiable snapshot of the elements. Later structural edits to the original list do not change the snapshot. This is a shallow copy: mutable element objects can still be shared.

Collections.unmodifiableList wraps a live view of the original list. It prevents edits through that view but still reflects edits through the original reference. Neither operation makes arbitrary element objects deeply immutable.

lessons.title: Join a worker before observing its result
lessons.summary: If the worker assigns 11, what prints after join?
explanation: Runnable is a functional interface whose run method takes no arguments and returns no value. The empty () in () -> introduces a zero-argument lambda. Thread.start schedules the Runnable on another thread; run called directly is just an ordinary method call. join waits for the started worker to terminate. The lambda stores into a one-element array because captured local bindings cannot be reassigned.

After a successful join, the worker actions happen-before the following read. Reading before join would lack this guarantee. Sleeping for a guessed duration is not a substitute. main declares InterruptedException instead of ignoring a failed join.
Expected output or behavior: 7. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain why moving the read before join would invalidate the guaranteed answer; do not use sleep as a repair. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

lessons.title: Protect shared state with synchronization

lessons.title: Update a counter atomically

lessons.title: Cooperate with interruption and cancellation
lessons.summary: If main opens the gate instead of interrupting, what prints?
explanation: interrupt requests that a thread respond; it is not a forced kill. A blocking interruptible operation such as CountDownLatch.await throws InterruptedException when interrupted, clearing the interrupt status. A worker can clean up and exit; when it cannot propagate the exception, restoring the status preserves the signal.

A CountDownLatch starts with a count; countDown reduces it, and await waits until it reaches zero. The started latch tells main that the worker has reached its setup. The never-opened gate keeps it waiting until interrupted. The worker catches the exception, records cancellation and restores its status before returning. main joins before reading the result; no race with guessed sleep timing is used.
Expected output or behavior: cancelled. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Explain why restoring interrupt status is different from forcing another thread to stop. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

lessons.title: Recognize reachability and resource ownership
lessons.summary: If the body calls use twice, what still happens?
explanation: Garbage collection reclaims memory of objects no longer reachable, at an unspecified time. It is not a reliable way to close files or other external resources. AutoCloseable lets a resource owner release them deterministically with try-with-resources.

This toy resource prints on close so the ownership boundary is visible without opening a real file. close runs on normal or exceptional block exit. A still-reachable reference and a closed resource are separate concepts; closing is not object deletion.

lessons.title: Build a resilient study-session model
lessons.summary: With target 3 and the same four commands, what prints?
explanation: A Session record stores completed and target counts. The compact constructor is written Session { ... } without a parameter list. Its component parameters are available inside, and implicit field assignments happen after the body completes normally. It rejects negative completed values, nonpositive targets and completed values above target. The step method returns a new valid Session; it does not mutate an existing record.

A done command increments only below target. Unknown commands leave the state unchanged. The fixed command list makes this a bounded study-session model, not a persistent tracker or concurrent service. Repeated done commands cannot exceed the target; invalid construction fails immediately.
